message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 15 mph if a school bus is stopped). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all ages. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• For commercial drivers: 0.04 %.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Stop signs: stop, yield to traffic on the right.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is ≤ 200 ft. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Towing requires a valid license and registration.
• Vehicles must display a valid license plate and registration sticker. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Stop in both directions until the bus’s stop sign is down. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in some counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Points are added to your driving record.
• Accumulating points can lead to license suspension.
• Fines vary by violation and county. | ### Where to Find Official Texts - **Texas Transportation Code** – Chapter 545 (Traffic Rules) and Chapter 545.1 (Traffic Regulations). - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – provides downloadable handbooks and updates. - **Texas Legislature Online** – searchable database of statutes. ### Quick Tips - Always check local ordinances; some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have stricter speed limits or additional rules. - Keep your driver’s license and registration up to date; Texas requires renewal every 2–4 years depending on your age. - If you’re a new driver, consider enrolling in a defensive driving course; it can reduce insurance rates and help avoid points. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular traffic situation!
